utterance: Hi Mark, I'm the doctor today. I can see you've been dealing with a cough and fever for a few days. Tell me in your own words what's been going on — when did it start, and how have you been feeling?
reply: It started three days ago with a dry, hacking cough. I have been burning up on and off, and didn't have a thermometer, but I was roasting. Since yesterday I am bringing stuff up that is a rusty, brownish colour, even though it was clear at first. Also, there is a sharp pain low down on the right side, round towards my back, which catches me when I take a deep breath or cough, and that started yesterday too.

awards.label: Chest pain with breathing or coughing

utterance: That sounds unpleasant — the rusty-coloured phlegm and the sharp pain when you breathe are important clues. A few more questions: Have you felt short of breath or found it harder to breathe than usual? Have you had shaking chills where you can't stop shivering? And are you managing to drink and keep fluids down — any vomiting or diarrhoea?
reply: I only noticed getting puffed going up the stairs and on the way in from the car park, but sitting here I am alright. The first night I was shaking under the doona with my teeth chattering even though I was boiling, and there is no vomiting.

utterance: Now some background. Do you have any medical conditions — asthma, diabetes, heart or lung problems? Do you smoke or vape, and if so how much? And do you take any regular medications, including over-the-counter things?
reply: I have never had asthma or anything with my lungs, no heart problems, and I have never smoked.

utterance: Good. Do you take any regular medications or supplements, and are you allergic to any medicines? Also — any sore throat, runny or blocked nose, earache, or general muscle aches and headache with this? And has anyone around you been sick, or have you travelled anywhere recently?
reply: I don't take any regular medications, but I am allergic to penicillin because I came up in hives and my lips swelled when I was a kid, and it is probably not on my file since I have not needed antibiotics in years. I haven't noticed any sore throat, runny or blocked nose, earache, or general muscle aches and headaches, and I haven't been anywhere, just school and home.

utterance: That's really important — thank you for telling me about the penicillin reaction with hives and lip swelling. I'll make sure that gets recorded prominently in your file, because it changes which antibiotics I can safely use. Now I'd like to examine you, starting with your temperature, heart rate, blood pressure and oxygen level, then I'll listen to your chest.
reply: Right, let's just get this over with so I can get back to marking these exams.

finding: Normal chest shape. Breathing slightly fast; holds back on deep breaths on the right.
Expansion reduced on the right lower chest.
Lungs (front): Resonant. Lungs (back): Dull to percussion at the right base. Left base resonant. Elsewhere: dull at the right base posteriorly. Resonant elsewhere.

Lungs (front): Vesicular breath sounds. No added sounds. Lungs (back): Bronchial breathing with coarse crackles at the right base. Left base clear. Elsewhere: bronchial breathing and coarse crackles at the right base posteriorly. Vesicular elsewhere. No wheeze.

utterance:
Your observations and chest exam point towards a pneumonia — an infection in the lower part of your right lung. The signs fit: fever, shivering, rusty-coloured phlegm, pain on deep breathing, and I can hear crackles and changes over the right base of your lung. The good news is that you're otherwise well, your oxygen level is reasonable, and you're suitable to be treated at home rather than in hospital.

I'd like to confirm this with a chest X-ray today. Because of your penicillin allergy, I'll treat you with a different antibiotic called doxycycline, which is safe for you and works well for this kind of pneumonia. Before I sort that out — do you drink alcohol, and if so how much?
reply: I just have a couple of beers on the weekend, and none this week.

result: Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms. Other lobes clear. No pleural effusion. Normal heart size.

awards.label: Doxycycline 100 mg orally 12-hourly for 5–7 days (penicillin allergy)

dose: 2 tablets (1 g) up to four times a day, maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours

awards.label: Paracetamol for fever and chest pain

utterance:
The X-ray confirms it: you have pneumonia in the lower lobe of your right lung. Your heart is fine and there's no fluid around the lung, which is good.

Here's the plan:

1. **Doxycycline** — one 100 mg tablet twice a day for 5 days. It's an antibiotic that is safe with your penicillin allergy. Take the full course even if you feel better after a couple of days. Take it with a glass of water and don't lie down for half an hour afterwards, and it can make your skin more sensitive to sunburn, so be careful in the sun. Take it at a different time from any antacids or dairy-heavy supplements if you use them.

2. **Paracetamol** — two 500 mg tablets up to four times a day for the fever and the sharp chest pain. No more than eight tablets in 24 hours.

3. **Rest and fluids** — no work this week. I'll give you a medical certificate. Drink plenty, and expect the cough and tiredness to take a couple of weeks to fully settle, though the fever should improve within 2–3 days.

4. **Follow-up** — I'd like to see you again in two days to check you're improving, and we'll repeat the chest X-ray in about six weeks to make sure the pneumonia has completely cleared. At your age and as a non-smoker this is just a precaution.

Please go straight to the emergency department, or call an ambulance, if you get much more breathless, the chest pain gets severe, you cough up blood, you become confused or drowsy, or you can't keep fluids down. And if the fevers aren't settling after 48–72 hours on the antibiotics, come back to see me sooner.

One more thing — your record says "no known allergies", so I've updated it with your penicillin allergy. Any questions?
reply: Pneumonia? I can't remember the last time I felt this knocked about, but as long as I can get back to my classes soon.

utterance: Yes — pneumonia can knock even fit people around, so don't be surprised if you feel washed out for a week or two. With rest, fluids and the antibiotics you should turn the corner in the next couple of days. Just don't rush back to the classroom too early. Take care, and I'll see you in two days — sooner if anything worsens.
